title: LG UltraGear 27GP950-B
description: The LG UltraGear 27GP950-B is a 27-inch 4K Nano IPS gaming monitor running 144 Hz native with a 165 Hz overclock mode. It pairs a 1 ms gray-to-gray response with HDMI 2.1 ports, so consoles and PCs can drive full 4K at 120 Hz. DisplayHDR 600 certification gives it meaningful HDR headroom for a mid-range gaming panel.

demo.program:
import math
# LG UltraGear 27GP950-B: pixel density + uncompressed interface bandwidth estimate
w, h = 3840, 2160            # native resolution
diag = 27              # inches diagonal
refresh = 144        # Hz
ppi = math.hypot(w, h) / diag
# 10-bit color ~= 30 bits per pixel; rough uncompressed bandwidth
gbps = w * h * refresh * 30 / 1e9
print(f"PPI: {ppi:.1f}")
print(f"Uncompressed bandwidth @ {refresh} Hz: {gbps:.1f} Gbps")
need = "HDMI 2.1 / DP 1.4 with DSC" if gbps > 25 else ("DP 1.2 / HDMI 2.0" if gbps > 14 else "DP 1.2 / HDMI 1.4")
print("Interface class needed:", need)

description: Philips' 279P1 is a 27-inch 4K office monitor with PowerSensor that dims the screen when you walk away, cutting energy waste. USB-C delivers 90 W charging plus video over one cable. LightSensor auto-adjusts brightness to the room, and the built-in KVM shares peripherals between two PCs.

demo.program:
import math
# Philips 279P1: pixel density + uncompressed interface bandwidth estimate
w, h = 3840, 2160            # native resolution
diag = 27              # inches diagonal
refresh = 60        # Hz
ppi = math.hypot(w, h) / diag
# 10-bit color ~= 30 bits per pixel; rough uncompressed bandwidth
gbps = w * h * refresh * 30 / 1e9
print(f"PPI: {ppi:.1f}")
print(f"Uncompressed bandwidth @ {refresh} Hz: {gbps:.1f} Gbps")
need = "HDMI 2.1 / DP 1.4 with DSC" if gbps > 25 else ("DP 1.2 / HDMI 2.0" if gbps > 14 else "DP 1.2 / HDMI 1.4")
print("Interface class needed:", need)
